note: Curated starting XIs. Players are listed row by row, starting with the goalkeeper, then each outfield row from left to right as seen by a viewer with the team attacking up the screen. 'formation' must sum to 10 (outfield players). 'accepts' lists extra accepted spellings/nicknames; full names and surnames are accepted automatically.

lineups.blurb: Roy Keane and Paul Scholes were both suspended, so Beckham played centrally. Sheringham and Solskjaer came off the bench to score in injury time.
Three down at half-time. Hamann replaced Finnan at the break and Liverpool scored three in six minutes.
Widely rated one of the great club performances. Mascherano, a midfielder, played centre-back.
Iniesta scored in the 116th minute for Spain's first World Cup.
Ronaldo scored both goals to finish as the tournament's top scorer, three years after a career-threatening knee injury.
Leboeuf deputised for the suspended Laurent Blanc. Zidane headed in two corners.
Terry, Ivanovic, Ramires and Meireles were all suspended, which is how Ryan Bertrand came to make his Champions League debut in the final.
City's treble-sealing night. Rodri scored; Stones stepped into midfield from the back four in possession. De Bruyne went off injured in the first half.
La Decima. Ramos equalised in the 93rd minute and Madrid scored three in extra time. Xabi Alonso missed the final through suspension.
Messi scored twice, Mbappe hit a hat-trick, and Emiliano Martinez saved the day in the shootout.
Hurst's hat-trick, and the only World Cup won by England. Two Charltons in the same side - you'll need first names for those.
Salah scored a second-minute penalty and Origi came off the bench to seal it.
Ronaldo headed United in front and then missed in the shootout, before Terry slipped and Anelka's penalty was saved.
Coman, a product of the PSG academy, scored the only goal to complete Bayern's treble in an empty stadium.
Gotze scored the winner off the bench in the 113th minute, six days after the 7-1 against Brazil.
Materazzi equalised and was then headbutted by Zidane. Grosso scored the winning penalty.
Guardiola's first treble. With Abidal and Alves suspended and Marquez injured, Puyol played right-back and Yaya Toure filled in at centre-back. Messi headed the second.
Often called the greatest team ever assembled. Carlos Alberto finished off the famous team goal for 4-1.
Revenge for Istanbul two years earlier. Inzaghi scored both, the first off his shoulder from a Pirlo free-kick.
A third European Cup in a row. Bale came off the bench to score an overhead kick, and Karius had a night to forget.
Tuchel's side won it with a Havertz goal after Mount split the City defence.
Mourinho's treble. Milito scored both and left for Real Madrid days later.
A second treble in six years, with Messi, Suárez and Neymar all scoring across the campaign.
The first all-German final. Robben scored the winner in the 89th minute, a year after losing the final at home.
Mourinho's first European Cup, and his last match at the club before joining Chelsea.
An extraordinarily young side. Kluivert, 18, came off the bench to score the winner.
The first English club to win the European Cup, ten years after the Munich air disaster.
A fourteenth European Cup. Courtois made nine saves and Vinícius scored the only goal.
The first World Cup final decided on penalties. Baggio put the last one over the bar.
Mbappé, at 19, became the second teenager to score in a World Cup final after Pelé.
Maradona's tournament. He set up Burruchaga for the winner with three minutes left.
The biggest winning margin in a European Championship final, and a third straight major title.
Played a year late because of the pandemic. Italy came from behind and won the shootout at Wembley.
England's first major final since 1966. Shaw scored inside two minutes and it finished in penalties.
Rank outsiders at 150-1 who beat the hosts twice, including in the final through a Charisteas header.
Arsenal played most of it with ten men after Lehmann was sent off, and led until the 76th minute.
The second all-Madrid final in three years, and again Atlético lost it on the night.
Agüerooooo. City needed to win to take the title on goal difference and were losing 2-1 with two minutes of normal time left.
Trophy day. 5000-1 outsiders at the start of the season, champions with a game to spare.
The Mineirazo. Without the injured Neymar and the suspended Thiago Silva, Brazil conceded five in eighteen minutes.
The first all-Italian final, goalless across 120 minutes and settled by Shevchenko's penalty.
Three up at half-time in Istanbul, and beaten. Maldini scored inside a minute.
Ahead from the sixth minute, and beaten by two goals in injury time. Both hit the woodwork before that.
Zidane scored a panenka and was sent off for a headbutt in his last professional match.
A bad-tempered final remembered for De Jong's boot in Alonso's chest and Robben's miss.
A first final for a nation of four million, after three straight extra-time knockouts.
Two down and going nowhere, then Mbappé scored a hat-trick and it still was not enough.
Higuaín missed a one-on-one, Palacio lifted one wide, and Götze settled it late.
Holders, and outplayed. Eto'o scored inside ten minutes and Messi headed the second.
The first side to retain the Champions League. Ronaldo scored twice.
Mandžukić's overhead kick made it 1-1 before Madrid scored three in twenty-four minutes.
A fifteenth European Cup, and Kroos's last match for the club.
Zidane's left-foot volley off Roberto Carlos's looping cross, still the most replayed goal in the competition's history.
Barcelona's dream team taken apart. Baresi and Costacurta were both suspended.
Riedle scored twice, then Ricken lobbed Peruzzi with his first touch, sixteen seconds after coming on.
The Dutch scored from the spot before a German player had touched the ball, and still lost.
Wiltord equalised in the last seconds of injury time and Trezeguet won it with a golden goal.
A first trophy in forty-four years, and the start of everything that followed. Torres scored the only goal.
Ronaldo went off injured after twenty-five minutes and spent extra time coaching from the touchline. Éder won it.
Three down from the first leg and without Salah and Firmino. Origi scored twice, the second from Alexander-Arnold's corner taken quickly.
The manita. Guardiola's side against Mourinho's, and a five-goal exhibition.
Terry slipped taking the penalty that would have won it.
Ferguson called them the best side he had ever faced.
A final in their own stadium, lost on penalties after Robben missed one in extra time.
Klopp's young side, beaten by a Robben goal in the 89th minute.
Morata equalised against his old club before Barcelona pulled away.
Ahead until the 93rd minute, when Ramos headed in and the game turned.
Griezmann hit the bar from the spot, and Juanfran the post in the shootout.
Salah went off in tears after half an hour and Karius made two errors.
Guardiola picked no holding midfielder, a decision picked over for years afterwards.
Courtois saved everything. The kick-off was delayed half an hour by chaos outside.
Far closer than anyone expected. Lukaku headed straight at Ederson from six yards.
Lehmann was sent off after eighteen minutes; ten men led until the 76th.
A first European Cup final for the club, settled by a Frenchman from their own academy.
Chasing a treble of their own, and undone twice by Milito.
La Remontada. Four down from the first leg, and three goals in the last seven minutes.
Level in the last minute of normal time, then beaten by the most argued-over goal in the game's history.
Four days after beating West Germany 4-3 in the Game of the Century, and with nothing left.
Ronaldo was left off the team sheet, then reinstated, after a convulsion hours before kick-off.
Kahn had conceded once all tournament, then spilled Rivaldo's shot into Ronaldo's path.
Hosts and favourites, beaten by the side they had already lost to in the opening match.
Down to ten with all three substitutions used and half an hour to play.
Total Football, a penalty inside two minutes, and no German player had touched the ball.
Two down and level by the 81st minute, then Maradona found Burruchaga.
Roberto Baggio had carried them to the final, and put the decisive penalty over the bar.
The title won at Tottenham, on the way to a season without a single league defeat.
A rematch of Istanbul, and this time Milan held on. Kuyt scored late.
The first all-Spanish final, and an eighth European Cup.
A seventh European Cup after a wait of thirty-two years, settled by Mijatović.
Kahn saved three penalties in the shootout, twenty-five years after Bayern's last European Cup.
A second final in two years, and a second defeat. Mendieta scored from the spot inside two minutes.
Ravanelli cancelled out by Litmanen, then Juventus won the shootout.
The first Champions League final, and still the only European Cup won by a French club.
They dominated the first half and did not score. Madrid did, twice, after the break.
A first European Cup final, and a penalty conceded in the second minute.
Runners-up in the league, the cup and Europe inside a fortnight.
Giuly went off injured before half-time and the game got away from them.
Cruyff's dream team, taken apart by a Milan side missing both first-choice centre-backs.
A first World Cup, won at home. Kempes scored twice.
Rossi scored his sixth of the tournament having been banned from football two years earlier.
They had survived a shootout against France days earlier and had nothing left.
A third World Cup, from a Brehme penalty five minutes from time, in a final with two red cards.
Hosts and favourites, beaten by a Portugal side who had won one match inside ninety minutes all tournament.
Seconds from the trophy when Wiltord equalised, then beaten by a golden goal.

The other side of the most famous finish in Premier League history. QPR went 2-1 up at the Etihad with Joey Barton already sent off, and were surviving in the Championship-facing sense until Dzeko and Aguero scored in stoppage time. They stayed up anyway - Bolton failed to win at Stoke.
